learning_objective: The learner will identify the seven parts of a results summary from a description of how each looks, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** results-summary-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the seven parts of a results summary from a description of how each looks, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Results Summary, Effect Size, Difference of Means (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A results summary lists only the good news. (2) The limitations belong in a footnote. (3) The decision is separate from the results. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a report is a Remember-level task, and a picture of a one-page summary with its parts marked gives each a place. The quiz asks the learner to recognize a part by its look. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of a one-page report. At the top is a banner with a question-mark icon. Below it is a small drawing of two groups of figures joined by an arrow. Next is a grid of 24 small dots. Next is a pair of bars of different heights. Beside the bars is a ruler with one marker on it. Below is a triangle with an exclamation mark. At the bottom is a signpost with two arrows. The seven markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Question | The banner with the question-mark icon. | What the test set out to find out, and the hypothesis. | State the hypothesis as it was written before the test. | | 2 | Design | The two groups of figures joined by an arrow. | The versions, the groups, and the measures. | Name the one difference between the groups. | | 3 | Participants | The grid of 24 small dots. | How many students took part and finished. | Report how many were invited, agreed, and finished. | | 4 | Results | The pair of bars of different heights. | The means and the difference. | Report the gain and not only the post-test. | | 5 | Effect size | The ruler with one marker on it. | How big the difference is. | Say which convention you used. | | 6 | Limitations | The triangle with an exclamation mark. | What the test cannot show. | Name the small sample and the bundle of fixes. | | 7 | Decision | The signpost with two arrows. | What follows from the results. | Tie the decision to the hypothesis. | **Provenance:** The seven parts follow the chapter section "Results Summary". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels it "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 7 from the top of the page to its bottom. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 7 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 7 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 7 correct on the first attempt". At 6 or more it adds "You can read a results summary." Below 6 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with seven numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see a part of the summary." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of seven parts lists the same parts in the same order.
